expected_findings.rationale: No vegetarian or non-vegetarian symbol appears anywhere on this UK-formatted label.

A name and address are present ('Made in the UK for Oakfield Bakers Ltd, 22 Mill Lane, Leeds...'); whether 'Made ... for ...' counts as one of the named qualifying phrases is a genuine judgement call.
No FSSAI logo or licence number appears anywhere.
Only a UK-style best before date is present. India requires both a date of manufacture or packaging and an expiry or use by date; best before alone does not satisfy this.
The product is marked imported, but no importer name and address in India is declared, only the UK manufacturer address.
No name and address of an importer in India appears anywhere on the label, only the overseas manufacturer's address.
Wheat and milk are present as allergens, but the label uses UK-style in-list capitalisation rather than a separate Contains statement, which India's rule requires.

trap: A system that is not genuinely jurisdiction-aware might reuse a judgement it already made for the identical label under UK-001 and default everything to PASS, or might be confused by the in-list allergen emphasis and treat it as satisfying India's separate-statement requirement.
notes: Paired with UK-005, which evaluates the mirror-image case. Same underlying label design as UK-001, different jurisdiction, genuinely different correct answer on several rules. This is the dedicated cross-jurisdiction difference case.
